meta.purpose: The decisions this project turns on, and for each one: what is already known and from where, what is not known, the specific action that would find it out, who can perform that action, what it costs, and what the site does in the meantime. A decision listed here as open is not blocked by caution; it is blocked by a missing artefact, and the artefact is named.
meta.relationship_to_questions: questions/index.html is the question register: what is known and what is missing, per question. This file is the decision view of the same evidence, and it adds the three columns a question register does not carry: who can settle it, what finding out costs, and what the site ships while the answer is outstanding. Each row cross-references the questions it rests on.
meta.rule: Nothing here is a forecast. Where a decision cannot be made, the row says what is missing rather than substituting a guess. Where a default exists it is the one the site already ships with, so nothing stalls while the question is open.

decisions.decision: Should the site show prices, star ratings and review counts?
decisions.what_we_have: Program Policies §2(b) permits price and availability only where Amazon serves the link carrying that data, or where it arrives through the Creators API or PA API. Amazon's own documentation now records PA-API 5 as deprecated and returning 403, and lists the Creators API prerequisites as Associates enrolment plus at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days. A separate clause in the same section requires that a comparison-format price display also show the lowest used price.
decisions.what_we_lack: Nothing that would change the answer. This one is decidable today.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Nothing to find out. The rule is published and was read directly on 2026-11-20.
decisions.default: No prices, no ratings, no review counts. The comparison table keeps its blank columns and says why.
decisions.decided: Yes — no, and it is not close

decisions.decision: Are the five supplied links the products the owner meant to promote?
decisions.what_we_have: All five links were opened on 2026-11-20 and each reached a live listing: B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DHZTCNR5, B0DZFD6R9Z. The listing titles and category breadcrumbs were transcribed on arrival.
decisions.what_we_lack: The owner's intended ASIN for each link. Every submitted path code is 9 characters and contains lowercase letters; every ASIN on arrival is 10. That is evidence the codes are short-link slugs rather than identifiers, so intent cannot be read off the link, and filling intended_asin with the slug would be an inference.
decisions.how_to_find_out: For each product, open SiteStripe in the Associates dashboard, copy the tagged link for the exact ASIN intended, and record the intended ASIN beside the observed one. About five minutes per product.
decisions.who: Account owner only — SiteStripe requires sign-in
decisions.default: The site describes the product each link actually reaches, labels the ASIN as observed rather than intended, and leaves the intended column null.

decisions.decision: Does a click on these links earn anything?
decisions.what_we_have: The tracking ID shopnow047c-20 was supplied. Program Policies §2(b) requires the Associates ID to appear as a URL parameter on each link, in the form XXXXX-##. The links were opened on 2026-11-20 and the arrival URLs carried lv, btn_type, gaOptInStatus, btn_ref, channelId and plpRedirect parameters. No tag parameter was observed.
decisions.what_we_lack: One tracked click in the Associates click report. Without it the site cannot say whether the short-link service applies the tag server-side after the arrival page, or does not apply one at all. Both remain possible; neither has been shown.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Click one link from the owner's own device, then open the Associates click report for that day and look for the click. That report is the only permitted source for this number. Request sub-tag Associate IDs in the same session so later attribution can be read per page rather than in aggregate.
decisions.cost: One click and about 20 minutes in the dashboard
decisions.default: The site says attribution is unconfirmed, on the disclosure strip and on every product record. No page claims a click will pay.
decisions.decided: No — and this gates every other decision on this page

decisions.what_we_have: On 2026-11-20 the link link.amazon/B0c8moW59 reached amazon.com/dp/B0DHZTCNR5, a ThermoMaven instant-read thermometer, and the title was transcribed. An earlier session recorded three attempts that returned only Amazon's continuity page, and a parallel session briefly recorded the reverse mapping for P-04 and P-05 before a later fetch agreed with the register.
decisions.what_we_lack: Nothing about identity — the register now agrees across sessions. What is missing is an explanation of why the same link returned different results on the same date, and a second independent observation on a different date to show the destination is stable rather than merely consistent today.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Open the link from a normal browser on the owner's own network, note the final URL, and re-check monthly. If it ever stops resolving, re-issue it from the Associates dashboard.
decisions.who: Anyone for a single check; the owner for re-issuing the link
decisions.cost: Two minutes now, two minutes a month
decisions.default: P-04 is published as a thermometer with its observed ASIN, and the disagreement is published rather than smoothed over.
decisions.decided: Yes for identity — no for stability

decisions.decision: What should the site write about next?
decisions.what_we_have: A set of question-shaped guides, each limited to what the listing titles state. A sitemap and an RSS feed that the build keeps in step with the guide list automatically.
decisions.what_we_lack: Any evidence about what readers want. There is no Search Console property, no analytics endpoint deployed, and no query data of any kind. Every topic chosen so far was chosen because it followed from the catalogue, not because it was observed.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Verify the site as a property in Search Console and submit the sitemap, then read the queries the site already appears for. Free, and the only source of real demand available before traffic exists. Deploying the first-party counter on the measurement page would add on-site behaviour to the same picture.
decisions.who: Account owner for Search Console verification; an agent can prepare everything else
decisions.cost: About 30 minutes to verify and submit, then a fortnight of waiting
decisions.default: No new guides are commissioned from guesswork. The cadence exists; the topics wait for evidence.
decisions.decided: No — and it should not be decided by instinct

decisions.decision: Who is the author, and on what authority does the site speak?
decisions.what_we_have: No product on this site was handled, cooked with, measured or tested. No byline exists. Every guide states plainly that nothing was tested, and the checker fails the build if a first-person test claim appears.
decisions.what_we_lack: A named person, and either first-hand use of the products or a stated reason the reader should trust the writing without it. The FTC's Endorsement Guides require an endorsement to reflect the honest opinion of the endorser, which presupposes an endorser.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Two honest routes and no third: buy and use one product and write from that, or name an editor and state exactly what they did and did not do. Inventing a persona is the one option that is not available.
decisions.who: Owner decision — it requires a real name and a real claim
decisions.cost: One product and an afternoon, or one name and a paragraph
decisions.default: Guides are written as checklists of questions, which is what can honestly be produced without access to the products.
decisions.decided: No — and it caps how much authority the site can hold

decisions.decision: Should the two published editions be merged into one?
decisions.what_we_have: Two editions have been served from this repository: the maintained set generated from _src/data, and an older parallel set. Both reached the same five ASINs independently, which is corroboration rather than conflict. The maintained build writes only its own generated files, so it cannot damage the other edition.
decisions.what_we_lack: A decision. Nothing technical blocks the merge; the editions use different brands and URL layouts, so merging means choosing one and accepting that the other's URLs go away or redirect.
decisions.how_to_find_out: No new information is needed — the reviewer chooses. The reversible half-step available meanwhile is a canonical tag on each duplicate pointing at the maintained equivalent, which consolidates indexing without deleting anything.
decisions.who: Owner decision; an agent can execute either choice
decisions.cost: Canonical tags about an hour; a full merge about a day including redirects
decisions.default: The maintained edition is what the front page, navigation and sitemap point at. Duplicates are proposed as S-15 rather than removed unilaterally.
decisions.decided: No — deliberately left to a human, with the cheap half-step proposed

decisions.decision: Should the analytics endpoint be switched on?
decisions.what_we_have: A client that implements the five specified events, uses no cookie and no browser storage, refuses to run unless an explicit opt-in flag is set, and honours Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control. A collector exists in the repository but is not deployed. GitHub Pages serves static files only and cannot host the collector.
decisions.what_we_lack: A privacy notice stating what is collected, why, for how long and who to contact. A host for the collector. A decision on retention and on consent.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Write the notice first, then deploy the collector anywhere that accepts a POST, then verify a test event arrives and that no cookie is set. In that order; the notice is the part that cannot be retrofitted honestly.
decisions.who: An agent can write the notice and the collector; the owner must host it and own the retention decision
decisions.cost: A day, most of it wording
decisions.default: Inert. The site measures nothing, and every traffic statement on it says so.
decisions.decided: No — deliberately, and the order of operations is written down

decisions.decision: Do the two thermometers belong in this catalogue at all?
decisions.what_we_have: Three of the five products sit under Home & Kitchen > Small Appliances > Fryers > Air Fryers. Two sit under Kitchen Utensils & Gadgets > Thermometers & Timers > Meat. The two thermometers also differ from each other: one is an instant-read probe, the other a multi-probe wireless unit whose own listing names air fryers among its intended uses.
decisions.what_we_lack: Nothing factual. The open question is editorial: whether the site is about air fryers, about cooking thermometers, or about both under one kitchen theme.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Search Console queries would answer this better than any opinion, because they show which of the two subjects actually draws readers. Absent that, the owner decides.
decisions.cost: Zero to decide, a day to restructure
decisions.default: Both stay, in separate sections. Neither thermometer is ever described as an air fryer.
decisions.decided: No — the site hedges, and the hedging is visible in the navigation

decisions.decision: How much should be spent on paid acquisition?
decisions.what_we_have: Program Policies prohibit purchasing, registering or using any Amazon Mark in a search engine, disqualify purchases arriving through a paid search placement, and state that Associates must not use their tags to claim commissions from another programme on the same traffic. The site has no measurement that could attribute a click.
decisions.what_we_lack: Nothing. The answer follows from the policy and from the absence of measurement.
decisions.default: Nothing is spent. Recorded as a suggestion so the refusal stays visible after the reasoning is forgotten.

decisions.decision: Can the AI-generated imagery stay on the site?
decisions.what_we_have: Every photograph is generated illustration and every use carries a caption saying it is not a photograph of that product. The review page lists each asset, the intent behind it and every page it appears on.
decisions.what_we_lack: Any official statement, from Amazon or from the FTC, settling whether labelled AI illustration beside an affiliate link is acceptable. The site's position is a judgement, not a citation: labelled is an editorial convention, unlabelled would be a deception risk.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Replace them with real photographs of the real units. That removes the question instead of answering it, and it needs the products in hand.
decisions.who: Owner — it requires the physical products
decisions.cost: An afternoon with a phone and a window
decisions.default: Illustrations stay, labelled everywhere, with the caption enforced by the build.
decisions.decided: Partly — the labelling is settled, the long-term use is not

decisions.decision: What does a commission look like in money and in time?
decisions.what_we_have: The rate card is behind an Associates sign-in and was not supplied. What is published and was read directly is the payment mechanics: commission income is paid approximately 60 days after the end of the calendar month in which it was earned, and the policy page publishes a Payment Minimum Chart with different minimums per payment method. The figures in that chart are deliberately not restated here — this site's checker fails the build on any currency figure in visible text, and a rule that cannot distinguish a programme minimum from a product price should not be given exceptions. The source link carries the numbers.
decisions.what_we_lack: The rate for the Home & Kitchen categories these products sit in. No rate is copied from a third-party source anywhere on this site, because a rate with a false provenance is worse than a blank.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Open the rate card in the Associates dashboard and record it with a date. Ten minutes.
decisions.default: The campaign ledger is empty, shows its columns and states the provenance rule. No conversion score and no revenue forecast appears anywhere on the site.
decisions.decided: Partly — payment timing is known, the rate is not

decisions.decision: Is the site even indexable where it is published?
decisions.what_we_have: GitHub Pages serves this repository from a subpath, so every internal link is relative and the checker fails the build on any root-absolute href. A sitemap and a robots.txt pointing at it are generated by the build.
decisions.what_we_lack: Confirmation that a crawler has fetched the site. Without Search Console verification there is no coverage report and no way to know whether pages are indexed, excluded or simply unfetched.
decisions.how_to_find_out: Verify the property in Search Console, submit the sitemap, and read the coverage report a fortnight later. A site: query in any search engine gives an earlier, rougher signal.
decisions.default: The sitemap and canonical tags are correct for the subpath. Nothing else can be settled from inside the repository.
